reason: Local prerequisite (Koerner Lemmas 14.9-14.10, statements only in the source). A complete elementary proof is recorded: total disconnectedness gives a basis of compact open sets; the tube lemma applied to the closed set {(x,y): x∈E, x+y∉E} gives a symmetric W with E+W=E; then F={x: x+E=E} is a subgroup containing W, contained in E, and closed because {x: x+E⊆E} and {x: E⊆x+E} are intersections of closed sets, so F is a compact open subgroup; open cosets of F partition E, and compactness gives finitely many. Examined deps are published topology items (def-subgroup, closed/compact items, translations, local compactness); no choice needed; no cycle. This discharges the only part of the Ko §14 chain that is elementary.
